units.title: Apply Standard Precautions consistently
units.lesson: CDC Standard Precautions are minimum infection-prevention practices for all patient care, regardless of known or suspected infection. They include hand hygiene, protective equipment and other measures. A reassuring history does not make the baseline precautions optional. Additional transmission-based precautions may be needed in particular circumstances; baseline and additional protections are different layers.
units.question: When do Standard Precautions apply?
choices: Only after a positive infection test
To all patient care
Only to the first patient of the day
units.explanation: They apply regardless of known or suspected infection status.
rationales: A test is not a prerequisite.
Time of day does not remove the baseline.

units.title: Gloves do not replace hand hygiene
units.lesson: Hand hygiene and gloves have complementary roles. CDC includes hygiene before and after patient care and after glove removal. Wearing gloves does not make contaminated hands irrelevant. For study, distinguish a protective barrier from reducing contamination on the hands themselves. This note does not replace a facility’s complete infection-prevention training.
units.question: Which statement about gloves is correct?
choices: They eliminate the need for hand hygiene
They are another name for sterilization
They complement rather than replace hand hygiene
units.explanation: Gloves and hand hygiene address related but distinct protections.

units.title: Cleaning is not the same as sterilization
units.lesson: Cleaning removes contamination and precedes effective reprocessing. Disinfection and sterilization are different processes; they are not interchangeable labels. CDC classifies reusable devices by their contact with tissues and calls for appropriate trained reprocessing. This concept lesson omits cycle parameters and device-specific operating instructions, which require the relevant validated protocol.
units.question: Which statement about cleaning and sterilization is sound?
choices: The words always mean the same process
Cleaning precedes appropriate reprocessing
A visible clean surface guarantees sterility
units.explanation: Cleaning is a prerequisite step, not a sterility guarantee.
rationales: Visual appearance alone cannot guarantee sterility.

units.title: Respect information and participation
units.lesson: WHO’s 2024 Patient Safety Rights Charter includes privacy, confidentiality, information and supported decision making. A useful learning case can preserve the concept without exposing identifiable patient details. The charter supplies an ethical framework; this chapter does not claim to reproduce every Indian legal requirement. Avoid placing private patient information in public content reports.
units.question: Which report best protects confidentiality?
choices: A public post with patient name and medical record
An anonymized concept description without identifiers
A photograph showing every identifying detail
units.explanation: An educational description can explain the issue without identifying a patient.
rationales: This preserves the learning issue while reducing identification risk.

units.question: A paper policy omits Standard Precautions when a patient reports no infection. What is the scope error?
choices: Baseline precautions apply regardless of known infection status
Precautions apply only after a positive test
A negative history proves every transmission route is absent
units.explanation: Reported status does not remove the baseline scope.
rationales: A positive test is not required.
The history does not establish universal absence.
units.hint: Known status does not define the baseline.

units.question: Which statement correctly combines gloves and hand hygiene?
choices: Hand hygiene remains relevant after removing gloves
Gloves make all later hand hygiene unnecessary
Hand hygiene and gloves are identical processes
rationales: Gloves do not remove the hygiene requirement.
A barrier and hand decontamination differ.

The device has been observed

Sterility is not established by appearance.
